title: Every Midterm Since 1946 Ended the Same Way
creator: BWB - Business With Brian
summary: BWB - Business With Brian walks through 80 years of midterm-election market history, covering every midterm since 1946 ahead of the 3 November vote, and stresses this is not a political video. He makes four points. First, a midterm year — year two of a president's term — is historically the weakest of the four for the S&P 500, averaging about a 5% gain, with a drop of at least 10% at some point in about two of three years, driven by uncertainty; this year has been gentler, with a biggest dip of about 9%. Second, in all 20 midterms since 1946 the S&P 500 was higher a year after election day, up about 14% on average, and usually already higher within three months. Third, a flip of the House or Senate did not break that pattern; the expected setup — a Republican president losing the House — last occurred in 2018, when the market fell about 15% into Christmas Eve before finishing up about 12% a year later. Fourth, tech and the Nasdaq have beaten the S&P in the year after 11 of 13 midterms, by almost twice as much on average, but also dip harder into the vote. He explicitly says this is not a reason to load up on tech before the vote, and that earnings and interest rates will matter more than the election. No stock calls are made in this video.
